newsitem.title: UK: National advertising on UK radio rises 18 percent.
newsitem.headline: National advertising on UK radio rises 18 percent.

text.p: National advertising on British radio rose 18 percent in 1996 over 1995, the Radio Advertising Bureau said on Monday.
The largest radio advertiser in 1996 was the government's Central Office of Information, reflecting greater advertising throughout the year by Army Recruitment, the Radio Advertising Bureau said.

The top 10 advertisers, as of October, were: the Central Office of Information, Dixons Group Plc, Coca Cola GB, Carphone Warehouse, Kimberly-Clark Corp, McDonald's Corp , Vauxhall Motors, Ford Motor Co, Coldseal, and Renault UK Ltd.

A year earlier McDonald's was the top radio advertiser in the UK, followed by Kimberly-Clark, Central Office of Information, British national lottery operator Camelot, Dixons, Coca Cola GB, Renault UK, Carphone Warehouse, Star Direct, and PolyGram UK.
The Radio Advertising Bureau said the four largest spenders in 1996 doubled their ad spending over 1995.
